reader.requirement: At --std 85 literal-1 of a sequential file's ASSIGN clause must be refused unless it is a 1985 nonnumeric literal (quoted, at least one character), so a numeric literal, any figurative constant (ZERO, SPACES, HIGH-VALUE, QUOTE, ALL literal) and the post-1985 literal forms are refused; implementor-name-1 and the literal's value follow the implementor's documented rules.

edition-consulted.switches: sortMerge1985 (SD file and DialectLevel < 2002) suppresses the deferred numeric and figurative-constant findings; for an FD file at 85 the findings are reported as at 2023
NULL is read as implementor-name-1 where the edition leaves it unreserved (85) and refused as the predefined NULL identifier where reserved
COBOL0900 introduction gates refuse the hexadecimal X"..", national N"..", zero-length "", concatenation and ASSIGN USING forms at 85

reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: yes: at 85 the 2002+ literal forms (X"..", N"..", concatenation, zero-length) and ASSIGN USING are refused by introduction gates, and NULL is an implementor-name; the nonnumeric/figurative refusal for an FD file is the same arm as 2023
reader.witnesses-cover: part: witnesses cover the zero-length literal, SPACE and the device-class list; not numeric literals, the other figurative constants (ZERO, HIGH-VALUE, QUOTE, ALL literal), the post-1985 literal forms, or a run after a failed OPEN

reader.notes: The grammar admits any literal and AssignTargetRule screens it at bind, deferring the numeric and figurative arms to FileControlKeyRules.Screen so the 1985 sort-merge entry (no such rule) is spared; for an FD file at 85 every violation probed is refused. Diagnostics cite §2023:12.4.5.2 SR4 at --std 85 (wording only).

refuter.evidence: All built-in figurative constants refused at 85 in every position, including the second operand of a list: LOW-VALUES, ZEROES, ALL ZERO, DISK ZERO, PRINTER SPACES (COBOL2645 'shall not be a figurative constant'), DISK 123 (COBOL2645 'shall be an alphanumeric literal'). But probe src/r5-sym.cob (SPECIAL-NAMES. SYMBOLIC CHARACTERS SYMA IS 66. ... ASSIGN TO SYMA) compiles and runs at 85 and at 2023 and writes the file syma.txt (runs/r5-sym-001): the word is read as implementor-name-1, not as the user-defined figurative constant the program declared. In 1985 a symbolic-character is a figurative constant (VI.1.3.3, level 2 list), and a COBOL word that is both a user-defined word and a system-name takes its class 'by the context of the clause or phrase in which it occurs' (IV.4.2.2.1 SR1b); the ASSIGN format offers both implementor-name-1 and literal-1 there, so the text does not decide. The tree's own determination for the analogous 2002+ constant-name case (DOC-A.1-71, kb/Work PB2500: 'the program's own declaration of the word wins') would make SYMA a figurative constant and SR3 refuse it; AssignTargetRule has no symbolic-character arm and no documented determination for it. cite.py: 'OK  §1985:VII.2.3.3 SR3  (2.3.3 Syntax Rules)  the text is in SR3'; 'OK  §1985:VI.1.3.3  (1.3.3 Figurative Constants)  the text is in the clause'; 'OK  §1985:IV.4.2.2.1 SR1b  (4.2.2.1 COBOL Words)  the text is in SR1b'.

refuter.corrected: Reading: if the program's declaration wins (as DOC-A.1-71 rules for constant-names), ASSIGN TO <symbolic-character> is a figurative constant and must be refused (UNDER-REJECTS, cause b, same at 2023); if the implementor-name reading wins, the verdict stands but the choice is undocumented. Needs a recorded determination.
